mainTopic: Consecrating a field during the יובל year: רב and שמואל, the ברייתא, and the yearly redemption price
overview: This amud continues a מחלוקת between רב and שמואל: if someone is מקדיש his field during the יובל year itself, does it become holy? רב says yes, and it is redeemed at the full price. שמואל says no. First רב knocks down שמואל's קל וחומר. A field consecrated before יובל never goes back to its owner anyway; it goes to the כהנים through הקדש. Then רב and שמואל argue over the פסוק 'וְאִם מִשְּׁנַת הַיּוֹבֵל': does 'from' include the יובל year or start after it? A ברייתא says a field consecrated in יובל 'is not holy.' רב first explains this as 'not holy with a deduction.' When that runs into trouble, he says the ברייתא follows the רבנן, while he follows רבי, who holds that 'from X' includes X. The גמרא then works through the math of 'a סלע and a פונדיון' per year and shows how it fits both רב and שמואל, depending on how the years of the cycle are counted. Finally, a משנה about not redeeming 'less than a year after the יובל' seems to support שמואל. The גמרא begins to answer for רב, and its explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רב rejects שמואל's קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: רב explains why the קל וחומר does not work, even according to רבי שמעון. A field consecrated before יובל never goes back to the owner. It goes to the כהנים, and they receive it from הקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב holds: In the end, does the field go back to the owners? No, it goes out to the כהנים, and the כהנים acquire it from the table of the Most High!
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers the קל וחומר that שמואל used earlier, and shows why it falls apart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל argued: if an already-consecrated field 'leaves' הקדש in יובל, then surely a field consecrated during יובל cannot become holy at all. רב says the field never really leaves holiness. It does not return to the owner; it passes to the כהנים, who get it as a gift from הקדש. So there is no strong base to build a קל וחומר on.

keyTerms.meaning: In the end, after all is said and done
The original owners
Priests
'The table of the Most High,' meaning property of הקדש that is given to the כהנים
They acquire

steps.confusionAlert: רב is not saying the field stays with the Temple treasury. It does go to the כהנים. His point is that the כהנים receive it as part of הקדש, so it never returns to ordinary ownership.

phrases.english: And Rav holds:
Ultimately, does it return to the owners?
It goes out to the priests,
and the priests acquire from the table of the Most High!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב סָבַר: סוֹף סוֹף לַבְּעָלִים מִי קָהָדְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues from the previous section, where שמואל's קל וחומר was presented.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects שמואל's קל וחומר, even according to רבי שמעון.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The קל וחומר assumes the field leaves holiness in יובל. In fact it passes to the כהנים through הקדש and never returns to the owner.

steps.title: What is רב's source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what source רב uses to show that consecrating a field during יובל takes effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רב?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for רב's positive source. This line sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 1 only knocked down שמואל's argument. Now the גמרא wants to know what actually proves רב's own position.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason or source?

phrases.english: What is the reason of Rav?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from defending רב to asking for his positive proof.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that רב relies on.

steps.title: רב reads 'from the Jubilee year' as including it
steps.stepSummary: רב learns from the words 'וְאִם מִשְּׁנַת הַיּוֹבֵל' that the יובל year itself is included in the full-price redemption.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the פסוק says, 'If from the יובל year,' and the יובל year itself is included.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: רב reads the פסוק as starting with the יובל year itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says a field consecrated 'from the יובל year' is redeemed at the full value. רב understands 'from' as including the starting point. So a field consecrated during יובל is holy and is redeemed at full price.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק (verse)
The יובל (Jubilee) year
Included

phrases.english: As the verse states: "If from the Jubilee Year,"
and the Jubilee Year is included.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words 'מִשְּׁנַת הַיּוֹבֵל' include the יובל year itself.

steps.title: שמואל: 'from' means starting after the Jubilee
steps.stepSummary: שמואל reads the same פסוק differently. It does not say 'in' the יובל year; it says 'from,' meaning starting with the year after יובל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל would say: Is it written 'If in the יובל year'? It is written 'from the יובל year,' meaning from the year after the יובל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how שמואל pushes back on רב's reading of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everything here depends on one small word. רב reads 'from' as including the יובל year. שמואל points out that the פסוק would have said 'in' (בִּשְׁנַת) if it meant to include it. To him, 'from' (מִשְּׁנַת) means beginning after it.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it written...? (a way of saying: it does not say that)
In the year
From the year

phrases.english: And Shmuel: Is it written "If in the Jubilee Year"?
"From the Jubilee Year" is written —
from the year that is after the Jubilee.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives שמואל's other reading of the פסוק רב just used.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רב's proof from the פסוק.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: 'From' does not include the starting point; the פסוק would have said 'in' if it meant the יובל year itself.

steps.title: What does 'after the Jubilee' mean for שמואל?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges שמואל. For רב, the next פסוק, 'וְאִם אַחַר הַיּוֹבֵל', fits well. But if 'from the יובל year' already means the year after, what does 'after the יובל' add?
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well for רב: that is why it is written 'If from the יובל year' and 'But if after the יובל.' But for שמואל, what is 'after the יובל'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks שמואל's reading, using the very next פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב there are two clear stages. The first פסוק is the יובל year itself (full price), and the second is the years after it (with a reduction). For שמואל, the first פסוק already means the year after יובל, so the second פסוק seems to repeat it.

keyTerms.meaning: It works out well (for one view), setting up a challenge to the other
That is why it is written
After the יובל

phrases.english: Granted, according to Rav,
this is what is written: "If from the Jubilee Year"
"But if after the Jubilee,"
but according to Shmuel, what is "after the Jubilee"?

steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's reading of 'מִשְּׁנַת הַיּוֹבֵל' as the year after יובל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the first פסוק already means the year after יובל, the second פסוק, 'אַחַר הַיּוֹבֵל', seems to add nothing.

steps.title: The year after the year after the Jubilee
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers for שמואל: 'after the יובל' means the year after the year after יובל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends שמואל by giving the second פסוק its own meaning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For שמואל, the first פסוק covers the first year after יובל, when the field is redeemed at the full price. The second פסוק covers the years after that, when a reduction is made. So the second פסוק is not extra after all.

keyTerms.meaning: The year after the year that is after (the יובל)

steps.whatToRemember: רב: 'מִשְּׁנַת הַיּוֹבֵל' includes the יובל year, so a field consecrated then is holy and redeemed at full price. שמואל: 'from' means starting the year after יובל, and 'אַחַר הַיּוֹבֵל' means the year after that.

phrases.english: After the after.
phrases.notes: He means the year that comes after the first year following יובל.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the second פסוק so it refers to a later time.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought 'אַחַר הַיּוֹבֵל' would be a repeat for שמואל.
steps.terutzMaskana: For שמואל, 'אַחַר הַיּוֹבֵל' refers to the second year after יובל and onward.

steps.title: A ברייתא says a field consecrated in the יובל year is not holy
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב from a ברייתא. It says a field may be consecrated before or after יובל, but one consecrated during the יובל year itself is not holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged רב: One may consecrate a field before יובל or after יובל. But in the יובל year itself he should not consecrate it, and if he did, it is not holy!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to directly contradict רב, who said consecrating a field during the יובל year does take effect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב held that the יובל year itself is included and the field becomes holy. The ברייתא says plainly that if he consecrated it during יובל, 'it is not holy'. On the surface, that is the exact opposite of רב.

keyTerms.meaning: One may consecrate, meaning give the field over to הקדש
The יובל year itself
It is not holy; the consecration does not take effect

phrases.english: They raised an objection: One may consecrate both before the יובל
and after the יובל,
but in the יובל year itself he should not consecrate,
and if he did consecrate it, it is not holy!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling how שמואל reads the פסוקים, the גמרא now attacks רב's position from a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that consecrating a field during the יובל year takes effect
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא explicitly says a field consecrated during the יובל year is not holy, which contradicts רב.

steps.title: רב: It is holy, just not redeemed with a deduction
steps.stepSummary: רב explains that 'not holy' only means it cannot be redeemed with the year-by-year deduction. It is holy, and he pays the full fifty סלעים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב can tell you: It is not holy for the purpose of the deduction. But it is holy, and he pays fifty.
steps.whatsHappening: רב reinterprets the ברייתא so it no longer contradicts him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the redemption price is reduced for each year that has passed toward יובל (גירוע). רב says the ברייתא only means that this reduced price does not apply. The field really is holy, and it is redeemed at the full price of fifty סלעים.

keyTerms.meaning: The deduction, a lower price based on the years already gone
Fifty סלעים, the full fixed price for a field's redemption
They give, meaning he pays

phrases.english: רב can say to you:
it is not holy with a deduction,
phrases.notes: He means it does not become holy in a way that lets it be redeemed at the reduced price.

phrases.english: but it is holy, and one gives fifty.
phrases.notes: Fifty סלעים for each field big enough to sow a כור of barley.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the ברייתא in step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the ברייתא's wording ('not holy' means not holy with a deduction)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא means the consecration has no effect at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: The consecration works; only the deduction does not apply, so the full fifty is paid.

steps.title: That answer clashes with the rule about the last two years
steps.stepSummary: If 'not holy' means 'not with a deduction', then 'before יובל' must mean holy with a deduction, even right before יובל. But רב and שמואל both said there is no deduction in the last two years before יובל!
steps.simpleTranslation: This implies that before יובל it is holy and redeemed with a deduction. But רב and שמואל both say: one cannot consecrate a field to be redeemed with a deduction less than two years before יובל!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רב's answer leads to a conclusion that contradicts his own ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ברייתא contrasts 'during יובל = no deduction' with 'before יובל', then 'before יובל' must mean 'with a deduction', with no limit. But רב himself, together with שמואל, ruled that in the last two years before יובל there is no deduction. So the ברייתא, as רב explained it, does not fit רב's own rule.

keyTerms.meaning: By implication, meaning from this we can infer
To be redeemed, bought back from הקדש
Both of them
Less than two years before יובל

steps.confusionAlert: This challenge is not against the idea that the field is holy during יובל. It is against the explanation רב just gave, because of what that explanation implies about the years before יובל.

phrases.english: By implication, before the יובל
it is holy to be redeemed with a deduction,
but don't רב and שמואל both say:
one does not consecrate to be redeemed with a deduction
less than two years before!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּלָל דְּלִפְנֵי הַיּוֹבֵל קְדוֹשָׁה לִיגָּאֵל בְּגֵירוּעַ, וְהָא רַב וּשְׁמוּאֵל דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in step 8 by pulling out what it implies.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's explanation that 'not holy' means 'not holy with a deduction'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The explanation implies that a deduction applies right up to יובל, which contradicts רב and שמואל's rule that there is no deduction in the last two years.

steps.title: רב: The ברייתא follows the רבנן, but I follow רבי
steps.stepSummary: רב drops his earlier explanation. He says the ברייתא follows the רבנן, while he follows רבי, who holds that 'from the first' includes the first. So 'from the יובל year' includes the יובל year.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב can tell you: Whose view is this ברייתא? It is the רבנן. But I follow רבי, who says: 'first' means the first day is included, and 'seventh' means the seventh day is included. Here too, 'from the year' means the יובל year is included.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives a new answer: he admits the ברייתא disagrees with him, and says he follows a different תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of reinterpreting the ברייתא, רב says it reflects the רבנן, who hold that 'from X' does not include X. רבי, based on the פסוק about חמץ, holds that the boundary days are included. רב applies רבי's rule to 'from the יובל year', so the יובל year is included, and a field consecrated then is holy.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose view is this?
The Sages, the majority view of the תנאים
Included
Here too, the same rule applies here

steps.whatToRemember: רב's view rests on רבי's rule that 'from X' includes X. The ברייתא that disagrees follows the רבנן, who hold that X is not included.
steps.whyThisMatters: This turns the debate between רב and שמואל into a debate between earlier תנאים about how to read 'from' in a פסוק.

phrases.english: רב can say to you: Whose view is this?
It is the רבנן,
and I said my ruling following רבי, who says:
'first', and the first day is included,
phrases.notes: שמות 12:15, about eating חמץ 'from the first day until the seventh day'.

phrases.english: 'seventh', and the seventh day is included;
here too, 'in the year',
phrases.notes: This points back to the פסוק 'וְאִם מִשְּׁנַת הַיּוֹבֵל' from step 3.

phrases.english: and the יובל year is included.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְךָ רַב: הָא מַנִּי? רַבָּנַן הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives up the explanation from step 8, which step 9 undermined, and answers the original challenge in step 7 a different way.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the ברייתא to a different תנא (the רבנן) and aligning רב with רבי
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is a binding source against רב.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא follows the רבנן; רב follows רבי, for whom the יובל year is included.

steps.title: If רבי is right, why the extra פונדיון?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: if the יובל year is included, as רבי holds, what is the purpose of the extra פונדיון the משנה requires each year?
steps.simpleTranslation: If he follows רבי, what is the purpose of the פונדיון?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב's new answer using the price set out in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that to redeem the field, one pays a סלע and a פונדיון for each year. That extra bit is only needed if the fifty סלעים are spread over 49 years, meaning the יובל year is not counted. If the יובל year were included, there would be 50 years, exactly one סלע each, and the פונדיון would be pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: A small coin, one forty-eighth of a סלע
What is its purpose? What is it doing here?
If

phrases.english: If it follows רבי,
what is the purpose of the פונדיון?
phrases.notes: The משנה says he pays 'a סלע and a פונדיון' per year. That only works out if the price is split over 49 years, not 50.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 10 that רב follows רבי.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's reliance on רבי's view that the יובל year is included
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's price of a סלע plus a פונדיון per year assumes 49 years, which only works if the יובל year is not counted.

steps.title: רבי clearly requires the extra פונדיון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sharpens the question from Step 11: you cannot say רבי drops the extra פונדיון, because a ברייתא quotes him requiring a סלע and a פונדיון per year.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say רבי does not require the extra פונדיון, that cannot be. We learned that if someone consecrated a field two or three years before the יובל, רבי says he pays a סלע and a פונדיון for each year.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא blocks an easy way out of the question from Step 11. It shows that רבי really does require an extra פונדיון each year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 11 the גמרא asked: if רבי counts the יובל year, why add a פונדיון? Someone might answer that רבי simply does not add one. This step rules that out with a ברייתא where רבי himself says 'a סלע and a פונדיון.' So the question stands and needs a real answer.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say (the גמרא raises a possible answer in order to reject it)
A coin; the basic amount paid per year to redeem the field

phrases.english: And if you would say he does not hold it,
phrases.notes: 'It' means the extra פונדיון each year. The suggestion is that רבי does not require it at all.

phrases.english: but didn't we learn:

phrases.aramaic: הִקְדִּישׁ שְׁתַּיִם וְשָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים לִפְנֵי הַיּוֹבֵל,
phrases.english: If he consecrated it two or three years before the Jubilee,
Rebbi says: I say
he gives a sela and a pundeyon.
phrases.notes: This is per year that is left until the יובל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens the question of Step 11 by showing that רבי's extra פונדיון cannot be denied.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's claim (Step 10) that he follows רבי, who counts the יובל year
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבי counts the יובל year, the payment would be exactly one סלע per year, so the extra פונדיון that רבי explicitly requires seems to have no reason.

steps.title: רבי follows רבי יהודה's counting of the fiftieth year
steps.stepSummary: The extra פונדיון is explained: רבי agrees with רבי יהודה that the fiftieth year also counts as the first year of the next cycle, so a cycle really has only 49 years.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי holds like רבי יהודה, who says: the fiftieth year counts both for this cycle and for the next one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question about the extra פונדיון. It says רבי follows רבי יהודה's way of counting the years.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יהודה, the יובל year is also year one of the next cycle, so each cycle has only 49 separate years. The 50 סלעים are then divided over 49 years, which comes to a bit more than a סלע per year. The extra פונדיון covers that bit, so it fits רב's view that the יובל year is included.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds (this opinion)
The fiftieth year, which is the יובל year
Counts for this side and for that side, meaning it belongs to both cycles

phrases.english: Rebbi holds like Rabbi Yehuda,
who says:
"The fiftieth year counts for this and for that."
phrases.notes: He means the יובל year ends one cycle and also starts the next one, so a cycle really has 49 years.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in Steps 11-12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a further opinion that רבי holds, which explains the math
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If the יובל year is included in a 50-year cycle, the payment would be exactly one סלע per year, and the פונדיון would have no reason.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי follows רבי יהודה, so the cycle has 49 years. Fifty סלעים over 49 years needs a little extra each year, and that is the פונדיון.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the size of the yearly payment depends on two separate questions: whether the יובל year can be included, and how the years of the cycle are counted.

steps.title: For שמואל, must רבי follow the רבנן?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether, for שמואל, רבי must follow the רבנן. If he followed רבי יהודה, the math would give two פונדיונות per year, not one.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to שמואל, should we say that רבי holds like the רבנן? Because if he held like רבי יהודה, he would need to require a סלע and two פונדיונות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now looks at the same ברייתא from שמואל's side. It asks whether שמואל must say that רבי follows the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל holds that the יובל year itself cannot be used for consecrating. If רבי also followed רבי יהודה's 49-year cycle, that would leave only 48 years. Fifty סלעים over 48 years comes to a סלע and two פונדיונות per year, but רבי said only one פונדיון.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? (the גמרא suggests a conclusion and checks it)
Because if
He would need to (require)

phrases.english: According to Shmuel, shall we say
Rebbi holds like the Rabbanan,
phrases.notes: The רבנן disagree with רבי יהודה. For them the יובל year is not also the first year of the next cycle.

phrases.english: for if he held like Rabbi Yehuda,
he would need a sela and two pundeyons!
phrases.notes: For שמואל only 48 years would be left, so each year would cost a bit more.

steps.triggerLanguage: לִשְׁמוּאֵל, לֵימָא רַבִּי כְּרַבָּנַן סְבִירָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining the ברייתא for רב, the גמרא checks how the same ברייתא works for שמואל.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether שמואל must say that רבי follows the רבנן rather than רבי יהודה

steps.title: Yes, for שמואל רבי follows the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא confirms that, according to שמואל, רבי must hold like the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: It has to be so: according to שמואל, רבי holds like the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 14 with a firm yes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the רבנן's 50-year cycle, and שמואל taking out the יובל year itself, 49 years are left. Fifty סלעים over 49 years gives a סלע and a פונדיון, exactly what רבי says. So רב and שמואל each read רבי's math in a different way, and the ברייתא fits both.

keyTerms.meaning: By necessity; there is no other choice

steps.whatToRemember: For רב: the יובל year is included, and רבי follows רבי יהודה (49-year cycle). For שמואל: the יובל year is excluded, and רבי follows the רבנן (50-year cycle). Both views end up at 49 years, so both give a סלע and a פונדיון.

phrases.english: Necessarily, according to Shmuel,
Rebbi holds like the Rabbanan.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms the suggestion raised in Step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes. According to שמואל, רבי follows the רבנן, which leaves 49 years and fits a סלע and a פונדיון.

steps.title: The משנה's 'a year after the יובל' fits שמואל, not רב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the משנה that says one may not redeem a field less than a year after the יובל. This fits שמואל nicely, but seems hard to explain for רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'And one may not redeem less than a year after the יובל.' This works for שמואל: one may not redeem less than a year after the יובל, since the field cannot be consecrated before then. But for רב, what does 'a year after the יובל' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new challenge from the משנה. It supports שמואל and challenges רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For שמואל, a field cannot be consecrated during the יובל year, so it makes sense that redemption starts only in the year after the יובל. For רב, a field can be consecrated and redeemed during the יובל year itself. So why would the משנה wait until 'a year after the יובל'?

keyTerms.meaning: Redeem; buy back the consecrated field from הקדש
Less than a year
But (introducing the side that has a problem)

phrases.english: Come and hear:
"And one may not redeem less than a year after the Jubilee."
Granted, according to Shmuel,
"one may not redeem less than a year after the Jubilee" makes sense,
phrases.notes: For שמואל, the field could not be consecrated during the יובל year, so redemption only starts the year after.

phrases.english: but according to Rav,
what does "a year after the Jubilee" mean?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: וְלֹא גּוֹאֲלִין אַחַר הַיּוֹבֵל פָּחוֹת מִשָּׁנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the ברייתא of רבי to a new source, the משנה, to test רב and שמואל.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's view that a field cannot be consecrated during the יובל year itself
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: 'And one may not redeem less than a year after the יובל'
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's view that a field can be consecrated and redeemed during the יובל year
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the יובל year itself counts for redemption, the משנה should not wait until a year after the יובל.

steps.title: 'After the יובל' does not mean the year after
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to defend רב. It says 'after the יובל' does not literally mean the year after the יובל, and asks what it does mean.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you think it means literally after the יובל? What does 'after the יובל' really mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its answer for רב by rejecting the literal reading of the משנה. It is setting up the real explanation, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question in Step 16 assumed that 'after the יובל' means the year following the יובל year. The גמרא says that assumption is wrong. It then asks what the phrase does mean, and the answer comes in the next lines.

keyTerms.meaning: Do you think? (introduces a wrong assumption the גמרא will correct)
Literally; actually

phrases.english: Do you think it means literally after the Jubilee?
What does "after the Jubilee" mean?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts answering the challenge to רב from Step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the wording of the משנה (the full answer comes next)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'After the יובל' means the year following the יובל year, which would leave out the יובל year itself.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'After the יובל' is not meant literally. The real meaning is explained in the continuation.
